judge_assessment.explanation: I recomputed all 29 checks behind the twelve problems and every one matches: k=4 and 32 for the orange table; 48, k=12 and 120 for the cyclist; slope 2.5 from (0,0)-(4,10); 42 and 20 bags for c=3.5n; slope 1.5 and 15 L; k=1.5 and 13.5 cups; k=7 and the missing x=8; 12/30/54 for y=6x; 10 dollars on Plan A and per-minute 11/40=0.275 against 8/20=0.4 on Plan B; runner rates 4 and 3; 112.5 km and 7 hours; k=3, 105 dollars and 34 posters. The judge's representation-switching claim is fair — the sheet really does alternate table, graph, equation and context rather than grouping them. Two misses. The Quick Answers bank prints "10. 4, 3, —" although problem 10's third part is a VERIFIED compare with expected ">"; sympify cannot parse ">", so the em dash reserved for unchecked items is printed for a checked one. And nine of the twelve problems end with a plot or sketch instruction (1d, 2d, 4c, 6d, 7c, 8b, 9d, 11c, 12e) with no manual entry — the only manual entry on the sheet is problem 9(c)'s sentence — so the drawn half of this representation-switching worksheet is delivered as if it were machine-checked.

strengths_to_preserve: Problem 9 is the sheet's best item and is encoded correctly: Plan B's non-proportionality is not asserted, it is computed as two verified per-minute rates ((5+0.15*40)/40 = 0.275 against (5+0.15*20)/20 = 0.4), and part (c)'s explanation is properly declared {"type": "manual"} with a model answer in the key.

The key repeatedly says why a representation is the right tool rather than just using it: problem 2's solution notes that 10 hours is not in the table, "which is exactly why the equation is worth having", and problem 5's notes that 10 minutes lies beyond the graph's right edge — "the equation reaches where the drawing stops".

Problem 7's missing-value table is verified as two entries (k = 35/5 = 7, then solve 7x = 56 → 8) so the reasoning chain and not just the final number is checked; the key also confirms k against the other complete columns.
Each problem carries its own grid beside its work space, so the plotting task never depends on a shared figure a neighbouring problem could be read against.

root_causes.description: render_quick_answers._fmt sympifies string expecteds and falls back to the manual-only em dash on failure, so problem 10's verified ">" prints identically to an item nobody checked.
evidence: Confirmed mechanism: sympy.sympify('>') raises SympifyError and scripts/render_quick_answers.py line 61 returns "---".

root_causes.description: A drawn response — plot these pairs, sketch this line, draw the line through the origin — creates no obligation in verify.json, so a worksheet whose declared focus is moving BETWEEN representations verifies only the numeric half of nine of its twelve problems.
evidence: worksheet.pdf problems 1(d), 2(d), 4(c), 6(d), 7(c), 8(b), 9(d), 11(c) and 12(e) each require a plot or sketch on the supplied grid.
verify.json contains exactly one {"type": "manual"} entry, on problem 9, and its desc covers the phone-plan sentence only.
The key does describe the expected pictures in prose ("the four points lie on one straight line through the origin"), so the grading content exists and only the declaration is missing.

improvements.title: Render verified relation symbols in the Quick Answers bank instead of the manual-only em dash
improvements.proposed_change: In render_quick_answers._fmt, match relation strings ("<", ">", "=", "<=", ">=", "!=") BEFORE calling sympify and emit the typeset symbol ($<$, $\le$, ...). sympify("<") raises SympifyError and the except branch returns "---", the same glyph render_entry reserves for manual-only ids, so a verified relation and an unchecked item are indistinguishable in the delivered bank.
improvements.regression_test: Extend tests/test_render_quick_answers.py: render a verify JSON holding a {"type": "compare", "order": "relation", "expected": "<"} entry and assert the bank line is "2.~$<$" and that "---" appears only on ids whose entries carry no "expected". Fails today (the line renders "---").
improvements.expected_impact: Every compare/relation problem across the suite regains a readable bank entry, and the em dash goes back to meaning exactly one thing: nobody machine-checked this. On this sheet row 10 becomes "4, 3, $>$" instead of leaving the runner comparison looking unchecked.
improvements.risk: Low. The change is confined to one branch of _fmt; the only care needed is escaping the symbols for LaTeX math mode so "<" does not compile as a stray glyph.

improvements.title: Fail the build when a problem stem asks for reasoning and its verify entry is machine-only
improvements.proposed_change: Add a delivery-blocking lint that pairs the worksheet source with the verify JSON: scan each \problem block for an open-response demand ("explain", "say why", "say how you decided", "in one sentence", "what went wrong", "find her mistake", "describe", "sketch", "plot", "graph it") and fail the build when that problem id carries no {"type": "manual"} entry. SKILL.md should state the rule positively: a problem that asks for a value AND a sentence gets TWO verify entries, the machine one for the value and a manual one carrying the full-credit criteria, exactly as this run already does elsewhere. The keyword list must include the drawn-response verbs (plot, sketch, graph, draw, mark, shade), which is the form this case takes.
improvements.regression_test: New fixture pair under tests/fixtures: a worksheet .tex whose problem 3 stem ends "Explain in one sentence why ..." beside a verify.json whose id 3 holds only an eval entry. tests/check_prose_consistency.py must exit non-zero naming problem 3; adding {"id": 3, "type": "manual", "desc": ...} makes it exit 0. The test fails today because no checker reads the stem for open-response prose. Add a second fixture whose stem ends "Plot the four pairs on the grid" with no manual entry; it must fail for the same reason.
improvements.expected_impact: The gate chain's manual-flag count starts telling the truth, so a grader is told which written answers nobody machine-checked instead of reading "nothing is flagged for manual review" under a sheet full of explanation prompts. On curr-190 the manual count moves from 1 to 10, which is an honest description of a sheet where most problems end in a drawing.
improvements.risk: Keyword matching will flag stems whose imperative is decorative ("show your work"), so the lint needs a curated phrase list and an explicit per-problem opt-out, or authors will start declaring hollow manual entries to silence it.

case_summary: A polished proportional-reasoning set that really does interleave representations: tables to equations, graphs to unit rates, equations to values and back, and a closing print-shop item that runs table → k → equation → forward and inverse evaluation. All 29 checks reproduce exactly, the phone-plan problem grounds "not proportional" in two computed per-minute rates rather than an assertion, and its explanation is correctly declared manual. Two systemic defects survive the green gates. Problem 10's verified ">" prints as an em dash in the Quick Answers bank, the same glyph used for unchecked items. And nine of twelve problems end with a plot or sketch that no verify entry covers, so on a sheet about moving between representations the drawn representation is the one nobody records as needing a human.
